title: Switching Between Log and Exponential Form

blocks.html: Every logarithm statement is an exponential statement in disguise, and switching between the two forms is the main tool for working with What a Logarithm Is.

$$\log_b y = x \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad b^x = y$$ The base of the log is the base of the power, and the log itself is the exponent. Use this to evaluate logs, and to solve equations where the unknown is the input, the base or the exponent.
This is the definition of a logarithm, read in both directions. Because $b^x$ and $\log_b x$ are inverse functions, each form undoes the other: $b^{\log_b y} = y$ and $\log_b (b^x) = x$.

blocks.name: logscale
blocks.cap: $y = 2^x$ and $y = \log_2 x$ are mirror images across $y = x$: every point $(a, b)$ on one is $(b, a)$ on the other.

blocks.title: Switching forms
blocks.q: Write $\log_5 125 = 3$ in exponential form, and $10^{-2} = 0.01$ in log form.

blocks.title: Solving for the base
steps: A base must be positive, so $x = 7$.

blocks.html: Because the two forms undo each other, $b^{\log_b y} = y$ and $\log_b(b^x) = x$. For example $10^{\log 7} = 7$ and $\ln(e^{-2}) = -2$. These two facts are how you will solve exponential and log equations: apply the inverse to both sides.

blocks.title: Solving for the exponent
steps: $100 < 250 < 1000$, so $x$ is between 2 and 3 (a calculator gives about $2.398$).

blocks.html: Swapping the roles: writing $\log_5 125 = 3$ as $3^5 = 125$ or $125^3 = 5$. Keep the base as the base. A check: the base raised to the log must give the number inside the log.
